description: DISHA, an artificial intelligence initiative led by UN Global Pulse and implemented by the United Nations Office for Project Services, published building damage assessment outputs for the June 2026 Venezuela earthquake on HDX on 10 July 2026. Building footprints come from Google Earth AI's Open Buildings model and damage classes from Google Earth AI's damage assessment models. The files cover an area of interest in north-west Caracas and include footprint centroids, zero-shot results, final inference results and inference metrics. Coverage: the north-west Caracas area of interest only. Access: GeoJSON and CSV files on HDX. Licence: HDX lists it as 'other'; every use must credit Google Earth AI's Open Buildings and damage assessment models and DISHA, and may not use the UNOPS or UN Global Pulse names or emblems beyond that attribution; free. Caveats: the provider states that DISHA products are in a testing phase, may contain inaccuracies and must be validated independently before operational, financial, legal or policy use, and that they are provided as is. Simulation uses are a model-derived damage layer for comparison with radar and crowdsourced assessments of the same earthquake. Related records: the IMPACT and Conflict Ecology Sentinel-1 products, the Microsoft AI for Good Lab assessments and Google Open Buildings.
